$comment: Single source of truth for tier -> model routing in omp-dev-team. The `model-routing` extension reads this file (inspect the resolved tiers and effective bands with the /routing command). Tiers are WORKLOAD-SHAPED, not a single cost ladder: the cheap end is split into `nano` (pure lexical/checklist + input-bound scan -> the cheapest capable model) and `code` (cheap coding & agentic tool-use -> a coding-tuned cheap model). Agents declare a tier in their `model:` frontmatter via a provider-agnostic role (`pi/smol` -> nano, `pi/task` -> code, `pi/plan` -> balanced, `pi/slow` -> deep). Roles resolve through .omp/config.yml modelRoles (default Haiku/Sonnet 5/Opus; with copilot-preset, smol -> github-copilot/gpt-5-mini, task -> github-copilot/mai-code-1-flash, plan -> github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5, slow -> github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8). Using pi/ role aliases everywhere keeps agents provider-agnostic — no hardcoded Anthropic ids that break in Copilot-only environments.

nano.rationale: Pure lexical/structural pattern matching and checklist verification with NO code-semantics or tool-use requirement: naming, complexity, token-efficiency, a11y/WCAG checklist, progress/plan-adherence. Also the cheapest tier for input-bound scan work. Highest volume, runs in parallel at every checkpoint, so the output rate dominates the bill -> route to the cheapest capable model (default claude-haiku-4-5; with copilot-preset, github-copilot/gpt-5-mini at $0.25/$2.00 — ~55% cheaper output than the code tier).

code.rationale: Cheap work that DOES need code semantics or agentic tool-use: post-plan implementation of scoped slices (software-engineer build floor), build-phase test generation (qa-engineer), structural code-semantic reviews (js-fp, svelte), and codebase-recon (script-driven enumeration + grep scan; a FLOOR here, so the effort-band makes it SIZE-PROPORTIONAL during planning — trivial->code, standard->balanced, complex->deep — and the downstream judging agents run at deep). Route to a coding-tuned cheap model (default claude-haiku-4-5; with copilot-preset, github-copilot/mai-code-1-flash at $0.75/$4.50 — coding-tuned, agentic, beats Haiku on every coding bench tested). The plan + review gates protect quality, so the build runs cheap.

balanced.rationale: Semantic / cross-file analysis with balanced cost/quality: orchestration, spec-compliance, structural/test/concurrency/perf/doc review, architecture & domain DESIGN SYNTHESIS (architect, arch-review, domain-review — moved down from deep now that the balanced model is Sonnet 5, which reaches near-Opus quality on cross-file design/coding at ~40% lower cost than Opus), and most non-build team agents (product-manager, ui-ux-designer, tech-writer, platform-engineer, adr-author). Build-phase execution agents (software-engineer, qa-engineer) and recon sit at the cheaper code tier — the plan protects quality. Default claude-sonnet-5; with copilot-preset, github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5 ($3/$15).

deep.rationale: High-stakes SECURITY reasoning where a wrong verdict is expensive and Opus still leads Sonnet 5: security-review, security-engineer. (Architecture/domain design synthesis — architect, arch-review, domain-review — moved to balanced/Sonnet 5.) Route to the strongest model (default claude-opus-4-8; with copilot-preset, github-copilot/claude-opus-4.8 at $5/$25). Reserve it — most work does not need it.

effortBand.$comment: Effort-band routing (phase-aware bump-from-floor): the model is derived from the TASK SIZE (task-size-classifier, recorded by /scope in plan-gate state) and the PIPELINE STAGE, floored by the agent's declared tier. Put the effort into spec/plan: the size raises the band ONLY while planning (stage in bumpStages, default needs-plan); once the plan is approved, build/review run at the floor (a solid plan makes the build routine). effective = (stage in bumpStages) ? max(floor, sizeBand[size]) : floor. The agent tier is a FLOOR — never routed below it (high-stakes deep agents hold). No signal -> floor (static, retro-compatible). The ladder is cost-ordered [nano, code, balanced, deep]; `nano` is a workload-shape tier (lexical), so sizeBand starts at `code` (the cheapest implementation-capable band). copilot-preset is unaffected — the band picks a tier, then modelRoles resolves the model.
effortBand.$downshiftNote: Off by default. Set trivialDownshift:true to route agents ONE band below their floor on the fast path (downshiftStages, default trivial) for extra token saving — except a floor in protectDownshift (deep), which holds. This is the only case an agent goes below its declared tier; leave it off to keep the never-below-floor guarantee.
effortBand.$enforcementNote: advisory: the extension logs + warns on a dispatch whose tier != the effort-band tier (the orchestrator applies the rule). Set env DEV_TEAM_EFFORT_ROUTING=enforce to upgrade the warning to a block, or =off to disable the band entirely (pure static tiers, agent tier only).

notes: Keep the high-volume `nano`/`code` tiers on the cheapest capable models to limit token spend; reserve balanced/deep for work that needs them. The cheap end is split by WORKLOAD SHAPE (nano = lexical/scan, code = coding/tool-use) so neither over-pays for the other's model. Pair with the copilot-preset and token-diet plugins for further cost control.
